intent: Test whether denser sensing at the iteration 5 spread and look-ahead (seven sensors at 12 mm pitch, ±0.036 m, y=0.07 m, 16 mm footprint) reduces slalom line losses and s-bend max_error. The drivetrain (track 0.10 m, radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg) and body are unchanged from iteration 5, so the sensor count and pitch are the only variables. Expected: slalom line_loss_events below 1.85, slalom progress above 0.14, s-bend progress at or above 0.72, and oval finish at or near 95%. If steering_oscillation rises without a max_error change, revert to five sensors.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Seven sensors at 12 mm pitch over ±0.036 m reduce slalom line_loss_events below 1.85 and raise slalom progress above 0.14. (2) Oval finish rate stays at or above 90%. (3) If steering_oscillation rises sharply while max_error does not move, the bottleneck is controller gain, so the Integrator should retune kp/kd rather than the sensors. (4) If slalom line losses do not change, sensor density is not the slalom limit, and the next test is a small forward-offset change (y about 0.06 m) at the iteration 5 spread.
rationale: Scores so far: iteration 5 (5 sensors at y=0.07 m, x ±0.036 m, 16 mm footprint, track 0.10 m, radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg) scored 422.9, the best design. Iteration 6 (mass 0.4 kg) scored 422.1 with worse s-bend progress, so 0.5 kg stays. Iteration 9 (radius 0.045 m) fell to 389.9, with oval finish down from 95% to 80%, so radius 0.040 m stays. Iterations 7 (track 0.09 m) and 8 (outer sensors at ±0.045 m) both lost ground, so track 0.10 m and spread ±0.036 m stay. The remaining weak points are the s-bend (progress about 0.72, off-track exits, max_error pinned at 0.06 m) and the slalom (progress about 0.14, about 1.85 line-loss events per run). The slalom's losses look like sensor coverage and signal resolution on alternating bends, not reach. Adding spread (iterations 1, 8) and look-ahead (iteration 3) did not help, but no test has changed sensor density at fixed spread and look-ahead. This iteration changes only that: seven sensors at y=0.07 m spanning the same ±0.036 m, with a 12 mm pitch and the same 16 mm footprint. Tape stays inside the array across the same offsets, and the signal is averaged over more points, which should smooth steering on the slalom and s-bend. The change is one variable against iteration 5, apart from the sensor count the Integrator must match in the weights. Expected result: slalom line-loss events fall below 1.85 and slalom progress rises above 0.14, with oval finish held at or near 95%. The risk is that extra sensors add oscillation, as they did at y=0.08 m in iteration 3.
